brief: GS's financials desk notes Day 2 of earnings stays choppy: when AI rallies, Financials often trade inversely, and when AI capex funding worries resurface, that link reasserts. Rates round-tripped this morning's CPI print; cyclicals-vs-defensives basket is -6% off early-October levels, with the market's broader cyclical exposure catching up to what Financials have signaled for a month. Price action is questioning earnings growth, not credit quality, which the desk says ranks near the bottom of current debate topics (pipelines, capital, operating leverage, margin levers). Sentiment on earnings reactions is sharply negative, with the desk unable to find a clear reason for Citigroup's prior-day underperformance. On single names: BAC -5%, worse than guided despite a better 2027 NII guide, bulls citing NII upside versus bears citing thin 10.9% capital ahead of GSIB pressure; PGR -6% on worsening Personal Auto pricing; STT -6% on a top-line miss despite better NII/NIM, bears emboldened against its +35% YTD run; MS -3% on a wealth margin miss but capital-markets results better than feared; BLK flat, a clean beat with 11% organic fee growth and margin up to 47.8%, drawing almost no pushback.
